p.src: Seeing Xiapi ablaze, Lord Guan was alarmed. Several times during the night he charged down the hill, but each time a shower of arrows drove him back. At daybreak, just as he was preparing his troops for another charge down the hill, a rider suddenly galloped up. He looked and saw that it was Zhang Liao. p.src: Zhang Liao said, “Xuande’s fate is unknown, and whether Yide lives or dies is likewise uncertain. Last night Lord Cao captured Xiapi, yet neither soldiers nor common people were harmed. He sent men to protect Xuande’s family and forbade anyone to disturb them. Because he has treated them thus, I came especially to inform you.” Lord Guan angrily replied, “Those words are meant solely to persuade me. Though I now stand in desperate straits, I regard death as a homecoming. Leave at once. I shall descend the hill and meet them in battle.” Zhang Liao laughed aloud. “Would not such words make you the laughingstock of all beneath Heaven?” Lord Guan said, “If I die upholding loyalty and righteousness, how could the world laugh at me?” Zhang Liao said, “If you die now, you will incur three offenses.” Lord Guan said, “Then tell me what those three offenses are.”

p.src: Zhang Liao said, “When Imperial Uncle Liu and you first swore brotherhood, you vowed to share life and death. Now that he has only just suffered defeat, if you immediately die in battle and he later reappears seeking your aid, only to find you forever lost, would you not have betrayed the oath you swore in those days? That is your first offense. Imperial Uncle Liu entrusted his family to you. If you now die in battle, the two ladies will have no one upon whom to depend, and you will have failed the weighty trust he placed in you. That is your second offense. Your martial skill surpasses all others, and you are also versed in the Classics and histories. Yet instead of seeking to aid Imperial Uncle Liu in restoring the House of Han, you merely wish to brave boiling water and tread through fire to display the courage of an ordinary man. How can that be called righteousness? That is your third offense. Since you bear these three offenses, I cannot refrain from telling you.”

p.src: Lord Guan pondered awhile, then said, “You say I bear three offenses. What would you have me do?” Zhang Liao replied, “Lord Cao’s troops surround you on every side. If you do not surrender, you will surely die. A futile death would profit nothing. Better to surrender to Lord Cao for the present, then seek news of Imperial Uncle Liu; once you learn where he is, go and join him. First, you can protect the two ladies; second, you will not betray the covenant of the Peach Garden; and third, you can preserve your useful life. These are three advantages. You should consider them carefully.”

p.src: Lord Guan said, “You speak of three advantages; I have three conditions. If the Chancellor can grant them, I shall lay aside my armor. If he will not agree, I would rather accept the three offenses and die.” Zhang Liao said, “The Chancellor is broad-minded and magnanimous. What would he not permit? I should like to hear your three conditions.” Lord Guan said, “First, the Imperial Uncle and I swore to support the House of Han together. I shall therefore surrender only to the Emperor of Han, not to Cao Cao. Second, the two sisters-in-law must be supported from the Imperial Uncle’s stipend, and no one of any rank whatsoever shall be allowed to approach their door. Third, as soon as I learn where Imperial Uncle Liu has gone, be it a thousand li or ten thousand, I shall take my leave and depart. If even one of these three is lacking, I shall never surrender. Wenyuan, return quickly and report this.”

p.src: Zhang Liao assented, mounted his horse, and returned to Cao Cao, first relating the condition that Lord Guan would surrender to Han but not to Cao. Cao Cao laughed and said, “I am Chancellor of Han; Han and I are one. That condition may be granted.” Zhang Liao continued, “The two ladies request support from the Imperial Uncle’s stipend, and no one of any rank is to approach their door.” Cao Cao said, “I shall give them twice as much from the Imperial Uncle’s stipend. As for strictly barring outsiders and household members alike, that is but proper domestic discipline. Why should there be any question?” Zhang Liao added, “As soon as he learns news of Xuande, he will go to him, however far away he may be.” Cao Cao shook his head. “If so, what use would there be in my maintaining Yun'Chang? That condition is difficult to grant.” Zhang Liao said, “Have you not heard Yu Rang’s distinction between being treated as an ordinary man and being treated as a man of the realm? Liu Xuande has treated Yun'Chang with no more than generous kindness. If you, Chancellor, bestow still greater favor and thereby bind his heart to you, why fear that Yun'Chang will not submit?” Cao Cao said, “Your words are most sound, Wenyuan. I agree to all three conditions.”

p.src: When Lady Gan and Lady Mi heard that Lord Guan had arrived, they hurried out to meet him. He bowed below the steps and said, “It is my fault that my two sisters-in-law have suffered such alarm.” The two ladies asked, “Where is the Imperial Uncle now?” Lord Guan replied, “I do not know where he has gone.” The two ladies asked, “What do you intend to do now, brother?” Lord Guan said, “I rode out of the city and fought to the death, but was surrounded on an earthen hill. Zhang Liao urged me to surrender, and I set three conditions.” Cao Cao has agreed to them all; thus he withdrew his troops especially to let me enter the city. Since I had not yet obtained your wishes, I dared not decide the matter on my own.” The two ladies asked what the three conditions were. Lord Guan recounted each of the three conditions in full. Lady Gan said, “When Cao Cao’s army entered the city yesterday, we both thought we were certain to die; yet unexpectedly, not a hair on our heads was touched, and not a single soldier dared enter our gate. Since you have already given your word, why need you ask the two of us? I fear only that Cao Cao will later refuse to let you go in search of the Imperial Uncle.” Lord Guan said, “Set your minds at ease. I have my own plan.” The two ladies said, “Decide the matter yourself. You need not consult us women about everything.”

p.src: Lord Guan took his leave and led several dozen horsemen to see Cao Cao. Cao Cao came out through the camp gate himself to receive him. Lord Guan dismounted and entered to bow; Cao Cao hastened to return the courtesy. Lord Guan said, “I am a defeated general and am deeply indebted to you for sparing my life.” Cao Cao replied, “I have long admired Yun-chang’s loyalty and righteousness. My good fortune in meeting you today is enough to fulfill a lifelong wish.” Lord Guan said, “Wen-yuan conveyed my three conditions, and the Prime Minister graciously accepted them. I trust you will not go back on your word.” Cao Cao said, “Once I have spoken, how could I dare break faith?” Lord Guan said, “If I learn where the Imperial Uncle is, I shall go to join him though I must pass through fire and water. When that time comes, I fear I may have no chance to bid you farewell, and humbly beg your forgiveness.” Cao Cao replied, “If Xuande is alive, you must certainly go with him; but I fear he may have perished amid the confusion of battle. For now, set your mind at ease and allow time for further inquiries.”

p.src: Lord Guan bowed his thanks. Cao Cao gave a banquet in his honor. The next day, Cao Cao withdrew his army and returned to Xuchang. Lord Guan prepared the carriages and equipment, invited his two sisters-in-law to board, and personally escorted their carriage along the way. When they lodged at a posthouse on the road, Cao Cao sought to disrupt the propriety between lord and subject by making Lord Guan share a room with his two sisters-in-law. Lord Guan instead stood outside the door holding a candle, from night until dawn, without the least sign of weariness. Seeing him act thus, Cao Cao respected and admired him all the more. Upon reaching Xuchang, Cao Cao assigned Lord Guan a residence. Lord Guan divided the residence into two courtyards and assigned ten veteran soldiers to guard the inner gate. Lord Guan himself lived in the outer quarters. Cao Cao took Lord Guan to an audience with Emperor Xian, who appointed him General of the Household. Lord Guan thanked the emperor for his favor and returned home.

p.src: As they were speaking, a messenger sent by Cao Cao arrived to invite Lord Guan to a banquet. Lord Guan took leave of the two ladies and went to see Cao Cao. Cao Cao saw traces of tears on his face and asked the reason. Lord Guan said, “My two sisters-in-law wept bitterly from longing for my brother. I could not help but feel sorrow myself.” Cao Cao smiled and consoled him, repeatedly urging him to drink. Lord Guan became drunk. Stroking his beard, he said, “If I live unable to serve the state and yet betray my brother, I am a man in vain!” Cao Cao asked, “Yun-chang, have you ever counted the hairs in your beard?” Lord Guan replied, “There are several hundred, I suppose. In winter I usually wrap it in a black gauze bag for fear it may break.” Cao Cao had a bag made of silk gauze and gave it to Lord Guan to protect his beard. The next day, they attended the morning court and saw the emperor. The emperor saw a silk gauze bag hanging upon Lord Guan’s breast and asked him about it. Lord Guan reported, “Your servant’s beard is rather long, and the Prime Minister gave me this bag to contain it.” The emperor ordered him to let it fall loose before the throne, and it reached below his belly. The emperor said, “Truly, a lord of magnificent beard!” Thereafter, everyone called him the Lord of the Magnificent Beard.

Lord Guan reported, “Your servant’s beard is rather long, and the Prime Minister gave me this bag to contain it.”
The emperor ordered him to let it fall loose before the throne, and it reached below his belly.
The emperor said, “Truly, a lord of magnificent beard!”
Thereafter, everyone called him the Lord of the Magnificent Beard.

p.src: One day, Cao Cao invited Lord Guan to a banquet. As the gathering ended, Cao Cao accompanied him out of the residence. Seeing that Guan’s horse was thin, he asked, “Why is your horse so lean?” Lord Guan replied, “My unworthy body is rather heavy, and the horse cannot bear my weight; therefore it is always thin.” Cao Cao ordered his attendants to prepare a horse. Before long, it was led forward. Its body was the color of glowing charcoal, and its form was exceedingly powerful and majestic. Pointing to it, Cao Cao asked, “Do you recognize this horse?” Lord Guan replied, “Can it be Red Hare, the horse Lü Bu once rode?” Cao Cao said, “It is.” He then presented the horse to Lord Guan together with its saddle and bridle. Lord Guan bowed twice in thanks. Cao Cao said with displeasure, “I have repeatedly given you beautiful women, gold, and silk, yet you have never bowed to me; but now that I give you a horse, you are delighted and bow twice. Why do you esteem a beast above human beings?” Lord Guan replied, “I know this horse can travel a thousand li in a day. Now that I have fortunately obtained it, if I learn my elder brother’s whereabouts, I can see him within a single day.” Cao Cao was startled and regretted his gift. Lord Guan took his leave. p.src: Cao Cao asked Zhang Liao, “I have treated Yun-chang generously, yet he constantly longs to leave. Why is that?” Zhang Liao replied, “Allow me to sound out his feelings.” The next day, he went to see Lord Guan. After they had exchanged courtesies, Zhang Liao said, “In recommending you to the Prime Minister, I have never failed to put you foremost.” Lord Guan replied, “I am deeply grateful for the Prime Minister’s generous regard; but though my body is here, my heart remains with the Imperial Uncle, whom I have never ceased to remember.” Zhang Liao said, “Brother, you are mistaken. A man who lives in the world yet cannot distinguish what matters most is no true man. Xuande’s treatment of you may not have surpassed the Prime Minister’s. Why, then, are you set only upon leaving?” Lord Guan replied, “I know full well that Lord Cao has treated me with great generosity; but I have received profound kindness from the Imperial Uncle Liu and have sworn to die together with him. I cannot betray him. In the end, I shall not remain here. I must first render some service to repay Lord Cao, and only then shall I depart.” Zhang Liao asked, “If Xuande has already departed this life, to whom will you then return?” Lord Guan replied, “I would follow him beneath the earth.”

p.src: Yuan Shao said, “Let me consider it.” He then asked Xuande, “Tian Feng urges me to hold my ground. What do you think?” Xuande replied, “Cao Cao is a traitor who deceives his sovereign. If you do not punish him, my lord, I fear you will forfeit the great cause of righteousness in the eyes of the realm.” Yuan Shao said, “Xuande speaks exceedingly well.” Thereupon he resolved to raise an army. Tian Feng remonstrated once more. Yuan Shao angrily cried, “You men toy with letters and make light of warfare, causing me to betray the great cause of righteousness!” Tian Feng struck his head upon the ground and said, “If you do not heed my sound counsel, the campaign will end in disaster.” Yuan Shao flew into a rage and wanted to have him beheaded. Only after Xuande earnestly dissuaded him was Tian Feng instead cast into prison. Seeing Tian Feng imprisoned, Ju Shou gathered his clansmen, distributed all his family wealth, and bade them farewell, saying, “I go with the army. If we win, our might will reach everywhere; if we lose, I shall not even preserve my own life!” All wept as they saw him off.

p.src: Yuan Shao sent his great general Yan Liang as vanguard to attack Baima. Ju Shou remonstrated, “Yan Liang is narrow-minded. Though brave and fierce, he must not be entrusted with an independent command.” Yuan Shao replied, “He is one of my foremost generals—not a man whose measure you can take.” The main army advanced to Liyang, and Liu Yan, governor of Dong Commandery, sent an urgent appeal to Xuchang. Cao Cao hastily convened his officers to discuss raising troops against the enemy. When Lord Guan heard of it, he went to the chancellor’s residence and said to Cao Cao, “I hear the Chancellor is mobilizing his army. I wish to serve in the vanguard.” Cao Cao replied, “I would not yet presume to trouble you, General. Should the need arise, sooner or later, I shall send for you.” Lord Guan then withdrew. Cao Cao led out one hundred and fifty thousand troops, marching in three columns. Along the way, further urgent dispatches arrived from Liu Yan. Cao Cao took fifty thousand men ahead of the rest and went in person to Baima, where he encamped beside an earthen hill. Looking into the broad, level country before the hill, he saw Yan Liang’s vanguard of one hundred thousand elite troops drawn up in battle formation. Cao Cao was appalled. Turning to Song Xian, formerly a general under Lü Bu, he said, “I have heard that you were a valiant general under Lü Bu. Go now and fight Yan Liang.”

p.src: Song Xian accepted the command, took up his spear, mounted his horse, and rode straight before the lines. Yan Liang sat his horse beneath the commander’s standard, his saber held crosswise. Seeing Song Xian approach, Yan Liang gave a great shout and spurred forward to meet him. Before three bouts had passed, his arm rose and his saber fell, cutting down Song Xian before the armies. Cao Cao exclaimed in astonishment, “A truly valiant general!” Wei Xu said, “He has slain my comrade. Let me go and avenge him!” Cao Cao gave him leave. Wei Xu mounted with spear in hand, rode straight before the lines, and loudly cursed Yan Liang. Yan Liang made no reply. At their first crossing, he brought his saber down upon Wei Xu’s head and split him from his horse. Cao Cao asked, “Who now dares face him?” Xu Huang answered the call and rode out. After fighting Yan Liang for twenty bouts, he was defeated and returned to his own lines. All the generals trembled with fear. Cao Cao withdrew his forces, and Yan Liang likewise led his army away.

p.src: Having lost two generals in succession, Cao Cao was deeply troubled. Cheng Yu said, “I can recommend one man capable of opposing Yan Liang.” Cao Cao asked who it was. Cheng Yu replied, “None but Lord Guan will do.” Cao Cao said, “I fear that once he has won merit, he will leave.” Cheng Yu said, “If Liu Bei still lives, he must have gone to join Yuan Shao. If we now have Yunchang defeat Yuan Shao’s troops, Yuan Shao will surely suspect Liu Bei and put him to death. Once Liu Bei is dead, where else could Yunchang go?” Cao Cao was delighted and immediately sent a man to invite Lord Guan. Lord Guan at once went inside to take leave of his two sisters-in-law. They said, “On this journey, dear brother, see if you can learn any news of the Imperial Uncle.”

p.src: Lord Guan assented and departed. Taking up the Green Dragon saber, he mounted the Red Hare and, accompanied by several attendants, rode directly to Baima to see Cao Cao. Cao Cao explained, “Yan Liang has slain two generals in succession, and his valor seems irresistible. I have specially invited you, Yunchang, to consult with me.” Lord Guan said, “Allow me to observe him.” Cao Cao set out wine to entertain him. Suddenly a report came that Yan Liang was challenging them to battle. Cao Cao led Lord Guan up the earthen hill to watch. Cao Cao and Lord Guan sat while the other generals stood around them. Cao Cao pointed to Yan Liang’s formation below the hill: its banners shone brightly, spears and sabers stood thick as a forest, and its ranks were disciplined and imposing. He said to Lord Guan, “How mighty are the men and horses of Hebei!” Lord Guan replied, “To my eyes, they are no more than clay fowl and earthen dogs!” Cao Cao pointed again and said, “Beneath that standard and canopy, the man in an embroidered robe and golden armor, sitting his horse with saber in hand—that is Yan Liang.” Guan raised his eyes and looked, then said to Cao Cao, “To me, Yan Liang appears no more than a man displaying a marked head for sale!” Cao Cao said, “You must not take him lightly.” Lord Guan rose and said, “Though I am a man of little ability, I am willing to take his head amid his army of ten thousand and present it to the Chancellor.” Zhang Liao said, “There is no jesting in the army. Yunchang, do not be rash.”

p.src: Lord Guan sprang fiercely into the saddle, held the Green Dragon saber reversed, and galloped down the hill. His phoenix eyes opened wide and his silkworm brows rose on end as he charged straight into the opposing formation; the Hebei troops parted before him like waves split asunder. Lord Guan made straight for Yan Liang. Yan Liang was beneath his commander’s canopy. Seeing Lord Guan charge toward him, he was just about to demand his identity when the Red Hare’s speed brought Lord Guan already before him. Caught wholly unprepared, Yan Liang was struck by Yunchang’s single blow and thrust from his horse. In a flash Lord Guan dismounted, cut off Yan Liang’s head, tied it beneath his horse’s neck, vaulted back into the saddle, and rode from the formation with saber in hand as though passing through an empty field. The Hebei officers and soldiers were thrown into panic and fell into disorder without fighting. Cao Cao’s army seized the moment to attack. The dead were beyond counting, and vast numbers of horses, weapons, and other equipment were captured. Lord Guan galloped back up the hill, where all the generals congratulated him. He presented Yan Liang’s head before Cao Cao. Cao Cao exclaimed, “General, you are truly a man divine!” Lord Guan replied, “My feat is hardly worth mentioning! My younger brother Zhang Yide could take the head of an enemy commander amid an army of a million as easily as drawing an object from a pouch.” Cao Cao was greatly startled. Turning to those around him, he said, “Henceforth, if you encounter Zhang Yide, you must not underestimate him.” He ordered them to write this inside the lapels of their robes as a reminder.
